neighbours.label: a comma that sets off an appositive or clause right after the first noun phrase of a text, as against the same short texts written without punctuation
fire: My neighbor, a retired pilot, grows roses
Our dog, an old beagle, sleeps all day
Professor Lee, the chemist, gave a talk
The village, home to fishermen, is small
Her uncle, a famous chef, cooks for us
This town, founded in 1820, has a mill
Dr Patel, our dentist, is very kind
The river, wide and slow, runs east
quiet: My neighbor the retired pilot grows roses
Our old beagle sleeps all day long
Professor Lee gave a talk about chemistry
The small village is home to fishermen
Her famous uncle cooks dinner for us
This town has had a mill since 1820
Our kind dentist is named Dr Patel
The wide slow river runs to the east
